In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of L-ZGP as chiral counter ion for direct separation of enantiomers in methanol.
the separation of basic drugs and other amines using N-acyl derivatives of amino acids as chiral counter ions.
the separation of enantiomers of basic compounds using methanol as a mobile phase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the retention and enantioslectivity are governed by a combination of electrostatic, hydrogen bonding, pi-pi and steric interactions between the chiral selector (L-ZGP or L-ZGGP) and the solute.

the chiral separation of the basic analytes is based on the interaction between the positively charged nitrogen atom of the amines and the negatively charged carboxylate group of the chiral counter ions.

the retention of the amines increased with increasing concentration of L-ZGP in the mobile phase and decreased with increasing concentration of a base in the mobile phase, while the enantioselectivities decreased with increasing concentration and increasing hydrophobicity of the organic modifier.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the retention of the analytes is mainly governed by electrostatic interactions between the protonated amines and the anionic L-ZGP, and the enantioselectivities are determined by the chiral recognition between the protonated analytes and the L-ZGP.
the enantioselectivities are mainly governed by electrostatic interactions between the protonated amines and the anionic chiral selector.

the chiral counter ions L-ZGP and ZGGP can be used as chiral selectors for enantiomeric separation in methanol, and this is a promising approach for the direct analysis of chiral amines in biological samples without derivatization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enantioselectivities of the chiral selectors L-ZGP and especially L-ZGGP were found to be higher in methanol compared with acetonitrile.
it is possible to separate basic drugs directly using methanol as the mobile phase and N-benzyloxy-carbonylglycine derivatives as the chiral selectors.
enantiomeric separation can be obtained in a simple manner by using a chiral counter ion, a nonpolar solid phase, and methanol as mobile phase.
